content: Command tables have 4 quoted columns: Cmd., Sub cmd., Data, Description. Rows with empty Cmd. are skipped during load (formatting artifacts). Don't dedupe by cmd alone — use (radio_id, cmd, sub_cmd).

title: 9700-csv-rename
rationale: Source repo used civ-command-table.csv for the 9700; renamed to civ-command-table-9700.csv here for consistency with other radios, and updated civ-radio-capabilities.json to match.

name: strip-manual-page-refs-at-load
description: Manual page references ('See p. N', 'See pp. N and M', 'See pp. N, M') in the CSV Data and Description columns are stripped at load time in store.py via _strip_page_refs(), never by editing the bundled data/ CSVs. Regex: See p+p?. [\d,\s]+(?:and \d+)?. They are Icom-manual artifacts not meaningful in the API/UI. Covers both leading-prefix and trailing forms. Also strips 'See pp. 18 and 19' multi-page form.

content: Radio capabilities must be verified against both CI-V CSV command evidence AND the Icom UK product pages (https://icomuk.co.uk/Amateur_Radio_Ham and sub-pages for each radio). The product pages don't list every detail, but anything that DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the product pages is likely false and should be treated with high suspicion. Product pages are authoritative for hardware specs (type, power, modes, bands, architecture, display) and features not exposed via CI-V (HDMI, DVI-D, DPD, I/Q output, audio scope, FT8 preset, CW decoder, etc.). When a capability has no CI-V command but is confirmed on the product page, use command_evidence: 'Icom UK <model> product page'. When both CI-V and product page agree, cite both.

name: capability-types-and-evidence
description: The capabilities matrix (civ-radio-capabilities.json) contains three types of capability entries: (1) CI-V-backed — verified against CSV command tables, command_evidence cites specific hex commands; (2) Product-page-backed — hardware/UI features not exposed via CI-V, command_evidence cites 'Icom UK product page'; (3) Hardware-spec — string-valued specs (radio_type, tx_bands, rx_coverage, max_power, modes, receiver_architecture, display), command_evidence is 'Hardware specification'. The preamp capability was split into 'preamp' (internal, all radios true) and 'external_preamp' (9700 only, 4-value 0x16 0x02 encoding). The network_lan capability uses string values to specify what's available per radio (WLAN, Ethernet, false). Capabilities must be verified against both CSVs and product pages before adding or modifying.

title: capabilities-matrix-enhancement
rationale: Enhanced the radio capabilities matrix from 28 to 52 capabilities after a comprehensive review. Fixed 7 errors (7300 network_lan/ntp/dual_watch/qso_recorder, 7300mk2 dual_watch, 7100 touch_screen/sd_card) verified against CSV command evidence. Split external_preamp into preamp (internal, all 7 true) + external_preamp (9700 only). Broadened network_lan to use string values (WLAN/Ethernet/false). Added 7 CI-V-backed capabilities (vox, twin_peak_filter, digi_sel, wifi_bluetooth, psk_mode, contest_number, full_duplex), 10 product-page-backed capabilities (hdmi_output, cw_decoder, ft8_preset, dpd, dvi_d, iq_output, rx_antenna, audio_scope, satellite_tracking), and 7 hardware-spec capabilities (radio_type, tx_bands, rx_coverage, max_power, modes, receiver_architecture, display). External preamp for 7100 set to false — user-reported but no CI-V or product-page evidence found.

content: Every capability in civ-radio-capabilities.json has a human-friendly 'label' field (Title Case, e.g. 'D-STAR DV Mode', 'Twin PBT', 'DIGI-SEL') in addition to the machine-readable snake_case 'name'. The UI (app.js) displays label, falling back to name if label is empty. The Pydantic Capability model has label: str = Field('') so existing consumers without labels still work. Hardware spec capabilities (radio_type, tx_bands, rx_coverage, max_power, modes, receiver_architecture, display) are listed FIRST in the capabilities array, before all CI-V-backed and product-page capabilities, so they appear at the top of the capabilities table in the UI.

description: 7610 CSV dropped the '1A 02' memory keyer row (present in draft, missing from final civ-command-table-7610.csv) while civ-radio-capabilities.json claims memory_keyer=true for 7610 with command_evidence '0x1A 0x02' — data sources out of sync
resolution: Restored row "1A","02","see p. 13","Send/read memory keyer contents" between 1A 01 and 1A 03; convention: any capability command_evidence code must exist as a row in each claimed radio's CSV — cross-check before shipping
